newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to try to recover dead from Albanian sinking.
newsitem.headline: Italy to try to recover dead from Albanian sinking.

text.p: Italy pledged on Wednesday to try to recover the bodies of Albanians drowned when their boat sank in a collision with a navy ship that has overshadowed plans to deploy an Italian-led security force in Albania.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi announced the undertaking in parliament on his return from a surprise visit to southern Albania for talks on last Friday's disaster with the Balkan state's Prime Minister Bashkim Fino.

He said their meeting in the rebel-held town of Gjirokaster had removed "tensions and shadows" over the tragedy, which ignited anti-Italian hostility in Albania amid preparations for the multinational force.

Prodi promised a full and open investigation into the accident and quoted Fino as saying Albania regarded the sinking as a "tragic disaster...which cannot weaken the bonds of friendship between our two countries".

"He specified that it would be greatly appreciated in Albania if the bodies in the wreck could be recovered and if there could be some form of assistance for families affected by the disaster," Prodi told the Chamber of Deputies (lower house).
"I gave him my personal undertaking that this would happen," Prodi said, adding that he and Fino also planned to visit the rebel-held southern port of Vlore, from where the boat set out.

Tirana says at least 79 Albanians drowned below decks when the boat sank in the Adriatic following a collision with an Italian corvette carrying out orders to persuade Albanian vessels to turn away from Italian waters.
Many of the 34 survivors accused the Italians of ramming the boat, a claim Italy denies.
